speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail, starting with the pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities. When did these symptoms first appear, and have you noticed any other changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

The patient's history of rhinorrhea and low-grade fever followed by a "slapped cheek" facial rash that later spread to the extremities is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. I have sufficient information to confirm the clinical diagnosis without further testing.
